sentences.text: 95 to 100 percent of homes heating with oil, propane or electricity, and already running air conditioning, would pay less with a heat pump, a national study estimates.

assertions.text: For homes heating primarily with electricity, fuel oil or propane and with central or room AC, the study found 95% to 100% nationally would have positive bill savings, depending on heat pump efficiency.

validation.text: For homes heating primarily with electricity, fuel oil or propane and with central or room AC, the study found 95% to 100% nationally would have positive bill savings, depending on heat pump efficiency.

supporting.by: Wilson 2024 (NREL and LBNL), heat pumps for all?
supporting.note: Homes heating with electricity, oil or propane that have AC see lower bills in 95-100% of cases (median $300-$650/yr); 73-86% without AC; still 87-99% (propane) and 66-100% (oil) at 2019 prices.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

qualifying.by: CEE 2018, ducted and ductless cold-climate heat pumps in the field
qualifying.note: Measured cost savings averaged 33% against propane furnaces and 53% against electric resistance in Minnesota homes; oil was not tested, so the claim is supported for two of its three fuels.
qualifying.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

qualifying.by: Cadmus 2016, ductless mini-split evaluation (MA and RI)
qualifying.note: Mini-splits were cheaper to run than electric resistance and propane at all observed temperatures, but against oil they were cheaper only above a price-dependent break-even (about 32 F in 2016, 12 F in 2015).
qualifying.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

qualifying.by: Bernard 2024 (NBER), UK heat pumps and a time-of-use tariff
qualifying.note: In the UK, households previously on electric heating used less electricity after a heat pump, which supports the resistance-heat part; oil and propane are not tested.
qualifying.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

qualifying.by: Canadian Climate Institute 2023, heat pumps pay off
qualifying.note: Heat pumps use up to 65% less energy than electric baseboards, which supports the resistance-heat part; oil and propane are not modelled.
qualifying.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

resolved.explanation: The passage's population is homes that 'heat primarily with electricity', which includes electric furnaces and existing heat pumps, not only baseboards; the parent's s07 says 'electricity'. The 95 to 100 percent is the share of that wider group, and the Short gives no figure for baseboard homes alone. Not misleading in direction (resistance heat is the clearest case) but the population is stated narrower than the study's.
resolved.suggestion: Say 'oil, propane or electric heat' (or 'electricity', as the parent does) instead of 'electric baseboards'. The package hook and title carry the same 'baseboards'; the shorts review owns those.

resolved.explanation: 'where oil breaks the pattern' presupposes that oil breaks the pattern. That fact rests on the New England meters (Cadmus break-even temperatures), a claim outside this Short's package that the Short never spoke; in a Short the viewer has nothing else, so the close asserts a second finding without evidence.
resolved.suggestion: Make it a question, not a presupposition: 'Whether metered homes in Minnesota and New England agree with the model, and whether oil holds the pattern, is the subject of the full inquiry'.

resolved.explanation: 'linked above' points the viewer nowhere: on a YouTube Short the full video is linked in the description and as the related video below the player, not above it.
resolved.suggestion: Say 'linked below' or 'in the description', or drop the location and say 'the full inquiry' alone.

resolved.explanation: The study states that its bill results use winter 2021-22 energy prices and are 'very sensitive' to them: at 2019 prices the share of oil-heated homes with positive bill savings falls to 66 to 100 percent (propane 87 to 99 percent). The Short attributes the figure to the model, s06 says a model is exact about what it assumes, and the price year is not among the package's carried qualifications, so the sentence is accurate as spoken; but the 95 to 100 percent is the main case at one winter's prices, not a figure that holds at any price.
resolved.suggestion: No change needed for the Short; the full video is the place to say the figure moves with the price year, if an editor wants it said.
